data.standardized_narrative: During 2016 Syndicate 1861's gross claims reserves increased materially versus the opening position. Using the published gross claims development table, older underwriting years (2011-2014) show a net adverse development of approximately GBP 24.7m (12.0% of the opening gross reserves), driven principally by adverse development in Professional Lines and Marine, alongside a number of large manmade losses in Energy/Marine (Jubilee, Space X, Vermillion, Pemex). The report also notes a small net deterioration disclosed on a net basis (GBP 2.8m) - the difference versus the gross triangle likely reflects reinsurance recoveries and currency effects.
raw_causal_phrases: an increase in large claims across multiple lines in the year most notably on the Energy, Marine and Reinsurance classes, from the Jubilee (Tullow Ghana), Space X, Vermillion (Samir oil refinery) and Pemex claims.

data.data_quality_notes: Prior-year development (PYD) was calculated from the published GROSS claims development triangle (page 38) by comparing the latest estimate to the previous diagonal for underwriting years 2011-2014. The report also contains a narrative net deterioration figure (GBP 2.8m) which is net of reinsurance and therefore not used for the gross PYD - the gross PYD (GBP 24.745m) is materially larger, likely reflecting reinsurance recoveries, foreign exchange movements and other items. The 2014 year was reinsured to close into 2015 which may affect comparability; RITC activity was noted in the report and could distort development patterns for affected years.
